topic: Flow-sharp simultaneous CATE-curve sets under informative randomized-trial dropout. With finite baseline genomic profiles Z, a continuous predeclared prognostic score R, bounded survival, randomized treatment, censoring overlap, and profile-specific bounded nondecreasing Lipschitz residual-contribution functions, prove the law-sharp compact set of CATE curves tau_z(r)=b_1,z(r)-b_0,z(r)+s_1,z(r)-s_0,z(r). Derive a certified obstacle/min-cost-flow support representation, uniform grid Hausdorff error, and a uniformly shrinking whole-set confidence superset with simultaneous post-selection intervals for every eligible finite-VC genomic leaf. Reanalyse the ADJUVANT subgroup signs reported by Wang et al. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For any feasible s, setting q=s/u on positive-u cells and completing each censored event time at tmax with probability q yields the required contribution while preserving the observed censoring law; independent armwise completion gives sharpness and remains legal on zero-u contact sets. Each support direction separates into observed terms and arm/profile obstacle problems; grid versions are path min-cost transshipments, while Lipschitz-Hölder interpolation gives a candidate O(Lh+Mh^(beta wedge 1)) support/Hausdorff error. The obstacle set is sup-norm stable under perturbing u, and the duplicated two-profile witness is non-box. Existing pointwise dropout bounds, IV survival bounds, and generic support-function inference were checked without an estimand-level collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove one uniform theorem combining nuisance bands, robust obstacle optimization, and estimated covariate laws to attain the stated excess-Hausdorff and simultaneous selected-leaf rates through changing contact sets. EARLY KILL TEST: On ADJUVANT, predeclare R and the coarsest Z encoding the reported leaves, then propagate honest pilot bands through the obstacle program; if no leaf meets the mass conditions or every defensible-L sign interval contains zero, pivot to coarser profiles or a residual-mean sensitivity model.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the law-sharp joint identified set of all profile-specific CATE curves under informative trial dropout when each arm/profile residual-contribution function is bounded, nondecreasing, and Lipschitz, including score values where dropout mass is zero.

source_refs.claim: Derives covariatewise CAPO/CATE endpoint bounds under informative dropout and pointwise risk guarantees, but not a shape-coupled function-valued sharp set.
source_refs.author: Yuxin Wang, Dennis Frauen, Jonas Schweisthal, Maresa Schröder, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Develops sharp random-set identification for selectively observed outcomes and shape restrictions, but not informative-censoring CATE curves with score-indexed residual constraints.
source_refs.author: Arie Beresteanu, Ilya Molchanov, Francesca Molinari

source_refs.claim: Obtains partial identification of survival probabilities under arbitrary survival-censoring dependence with an IV, at an ATE/survival-probability rather than joint CATE-curve level.
source_refs.author: Yang Bai, Yifan Cui

open_problems.why_unsolved: Wang et al. bound each CATE value by differencing armwise CAPO endpoints, but those marginal intervals do not determine the jointly attainable curve set once monotonicity and Lipschitz restrictions couple score values. Sharpness requires one full-data completion that works simultaneously across scores and profiles. Moreover, the natural completion probability q=s/u is undefined where dropout capacity u vanishes, so the proof must establish observational irrelevance and legal completion on those contact sets while preserving randomization and the observed censoring law. Searches located pointwise dropout bounds, IV survival bounds, and general random-set methods, but no joint shape-constrained CATE-curve characterization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality between the observational-law-compatible CATE curves and a compact convex image of arm/profile monotone-Lipschitz obstacle sets, with an explicit full-data completion proving attainability on positive-u cells and legality on zero-u contact sets.

writing_exemplar.why: Its clinical-dropout motivation, transition from failed point identification to CATE bounds, and ADJUVANT audit provide the closest framing while the new target becomes joint and law-sharp.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Oncology dropout can depend on latent survival -> conventional CATE estimators become biased and point identification fails -> covariatewise partial-identification bounds restore robustness -> credible cross-score restrictions require the joint law-sharp CATE-curve set.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent latent completions by random correspondences, use measurable selections for attainability, and characterize the Aumann-expectation image through support functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require proving that every element of a convex function-valued region corresponds to an observationally equivalent completion rather than merely deriving valid marginal bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Use cross-fitted doubly robust survival signals, prove asymptotic linearity uniformly in the curve index, and calibrate a multiplier-bootstrap supremum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies uniform survival-curve limit theory that can estimate observed-law inputs to the sharp set, although its identification assumes conditionally independent censoring.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive a certified support-function algorithm for the shape-coupled dropout CATE set in which every support direction decomposes into arm/profile obstacle problems, grid problems are path min-cost transshipments, and the grid set converges in sup-norm Hausdorff distance at an explicit Lipschitz-Hölder rate.

source_refs.claim: Provides closed-form pointwise endpoint formulas and a SurvB learner, but no joint support optimization or certified discretization of a shape-coupled CATE set.
source_refs.author: Yuxin Wang, Dennis Frauen, Jonas Schweisthal, Maresa Schröder, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Uses optimal-transport linear programming and a dual representation to compute sharp DTE bounds under support restrictions.
source_refs.author: Ju Hyun Kim

source_refs.claim: Constructs shape-restricted nonparametric confidence bands through linear programs with controlled approximation error, but for a single regression function rather than dropout residual-capacity obstacles.
source_refs.author: Harold D. Chiang, Kengo Kato, Yuya Sasaki, Takuya Ura

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kim's transport program optimizes couplings with fixed marginals, while Chiang et al. encode shape restrictions for a single approximated regression function. Here the decision objects are arm/profile residual functions with pointwise capacities, censoring-induced obstacles, and simultaneous slope constraints. Strong primal-dual equivalence must therefore be rebuilt as a path-network transshipment with contact-set feasibility. A second missing step is two-sided set approximation: interpolation must control both support values and feasible continuous extensions to obtain Hausdorff, rather than merely objective-value, error. Searches combining informative censoring, CATE curves, monotone-Lipschitz restrictions, and min-cost flow found no occupied target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A support identity of the form h_T(v)=h_obs(v)+sum_{a,z}V_{a,z}(v), a primal-dual min-cost-flow certificate for every gridded V_{a,z}, and a uniform bound d_H(T,T_h) no larger than an explicit constant times Lh plus M h raised to the relevant Hölder exponent.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the destination problem and interpretable residual-survival bounds; the new narrative can begin from its pointwise formulas and explain why curve-level use demands an auditable certificate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Informative dropout leaves unknown residual survival -> pointwise formulas are tractable but discard cross-score restrictions -> shape coupling creates an infinite-dimensional optimization problem -> a flow certificate and controlled grid approximation make the sharp set computable and auditable.

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate sharp bounds as a transport linear program, prove a dual representation, and use primal optimizers to certify attainability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired support value is likewise an extremum of a linear causal functional over a constrained latent-completion set; its geometry changes to a one-dimensional obstacle network.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate functional shape restrictions and approximation-error envelopes into finite linear inequalities, then project the resulting confidence region through linear programs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest inferential LP construction in which a continuous shape-constrained object is replaced by a finite basis or grid while retaining explicit approximation control.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish uniformly valid whole-set inference for the sharp CATE-curve region when censoring probabilities, observed conditional means, and the score distribution are estimated and the obstacle program's zero-capacity contacts and optimal faces can change with the data-generating law.

source_refs.claim: Proves double robustness and a pointwise mean-squared convergence bound for learned CATE endpoints, not coverage or excess-Hausdorff control for an entire identified set.
source_refs.author: Yuxin Wang, Dennis Frauen, Jonas Schweisthal, Maresa Schröder, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Develops uniform bootstrap inference for optimal value functions using directional derivatives, with the feasible correspondence treated as part of the fixed optimization map.
source_refs.author: Sergio Firpo, Antonio F. Galvao, Thomas Parker

source_refs.claim: Gives Neyman-orthogonal, root-n Gaussian support-boundary inference for set-identified linear models, but not a function-valued obstacle set with estimated capacities.
source_refs.author: Vira Semenova

source_refs.claim: Shows ordinary bootstrap failure for merely directionally differentiable maps and supplies a derivative-aware resampling method.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.excerpt: Construct and validate one fully observable common-multiplier interval
Fang--Santos Theorem 2.1 gives convergence for directionally differentiable maps

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature establishes the two separate ingredients—directional inference for optimized value maps and orthogonal support-function estimation—but the dropout obstacle program has an estimated feasible correspondence because nuisance bands perturb its capacities and obstacles. The prior-proposal catalogue independently records the unresolved need for one observable multiplier calibration through degeneracy and a directional-delta route for nonsmooth causal maps. These components do not yet yield uniform coverage when zero-u contact sets or optimal-flow faces change: one must first characterize the support map's directional derivative as a critical-cone obstacle program, then combine derivative-aware resampling with one-sided nuisance bands, empirical covariate-law error, and discretization bias.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A random compact superset T_n^+ with uniformly honest whole-set coverage and an explicit uniform excess-Hausdorff rate, supported by a critical-cone directional-derivative formula and valid multiplier or test-inversion calibration along sequences with changing contact sets.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from identification bounds to orthogonal statistical learning exposes the precise missing layer: uncertainty quantification for the entire feasible curve set.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Informative censoring requires CATE bounds -> orthogonal pseudo-outcomes reduce nuisance bias -> pointwise risk consistency does not quantify uncertainty for the full feasible set -> uniformly honest outer-set inference is required near changing contacts.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive directional derivatives of marginal optimization statistics and bootstrap their sup-norm functionals uniformly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every CATE-set support direction is an optimized value function; the desired result needs the same uniform value-process machinery augmented for an estimated feasible correspondence.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace the inconsistent ordinary bootstrap by resampling an estimated directional derivative of a nonsmooth functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Changing active and contact sets make obstacle support values directionally but not fully differentiable, exactly the regime covered by their bootstrap diagnosis.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct Neyman-orthogonal support-boundary moments, cross-fit nuisance estimators, prove a uniform Gaussian approximation, and calibrate a multiplier bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired outer set is naturally indexed by support directions and must absorb flexible nuisance learning without first-order plug-in bias.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct simultaneous post-selection intervals for every mass-eligible finite-VC genomic leaf's treatment-benefit projection of the informative-dropout CATE-curve set, so selecting favorable ADJUVANT biomarker leaves cannot invalidate sign conclusions.

source_refs.claim: Reports data-driven positive lower DFS CATE bounds for ADJUVANT co-alteration subgroups without simultaneous post-selection coverage.
source_refs.author: Yuxin Wang, Dennis Frauen, Jonas Schweisthal, Maresa Schröder, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Selects genomic predictors and MINERVA cutoffs from 171 sequenced ADJUVANT tumors; several alteration cells contain only 12-33 patients and interaction intervals are wide.
source_refs.author: Si-Yang Liu, Hua Bao, Qun Wang, et al.

source_refs.claim: Provides semiparametrically efficient simultaneous inference for a supplied family of point-identified subgroups, not selected partial-ID survival projections.
source_refs.author: Waverly Wei, Maya Petersen, Mark J. van der Laan, Zeyu Zheng, Chong Wu, Jingshen Wang

source_refs.claim: Analyzes winner's-curse selection and develops conditional and hybrid intervals for an approximately Gaussian selected scalar target.
source_refs.author: Isaiah Andrews, Toru Kitagawa, Adam McCloskey

source_refs.excerpt: does not itself certify the required failure-relevant observable nondegeneracy
state precisely which temporal random-scale feature is new

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ADJUVANT analysis is exposed to multiplicity and weak-cell instability: genomic predictors and cutoffs were screened, some biomarker cells are small, and favorable lower-bound cells were subsequently highlighted. Existing simultaneous subgroup inference concerns prespecified point-identified effects, while winner-selection methods concern approximately Gaussian scalar estimates. Neither covers leaf-average extrema of a function-valued partially identified set whose nuisance-dependent obstacle program is estimated. The prior-proposal review adds the unresolved requirement that nondegeneracy be observable on the failure-relevant event. The missing proof step is therefore a uniform support-function linearization and observable leafwise variance/mass criterion over the finite-VC class, followed by selection-agnostic projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A family of intervals for every eligible leaf's lower and upper benefit projections with simultaneous coverage retained after arbitrary data-dependent leaf selection, plus a uniform shrinking rate indexed by leaf mass, VC complexity, observable variance, nuisance error, and grid error.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination-area motivation—molecular heterogeneity, competing genomic predictors, small biomarker cells, and actionable treatment signs—without implying that it posed the dropout-method problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: EGFR-mutant patients respond heterogeneously -> genomic profiling suggests candidate predictive alterations -> small adaptively chosen biomarker groups weaken confirmatory sign claims -> dropout-robust simultaneous post-selection intervals are needed before declaring a leaf beneficial.

method_exemplars.technique: Jointly target overlapping subgroup effects, derive their efficient influence representation, and exploit cross-subgroup covariance for simultaneous critical values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Eligible genomic leaves overlap and demand simultaneous inference; the new proof would replace point effects by lower and upper support projections.

method_exemplars.technique: Correct winner's-curse bias using conditional or hybrid projection intervals after optimizing over candidate targets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Reporting leaves with the most favorable estimated lower support bound is an optimization-based selection problem, although its scalar Gaussian law must be upgraded to a uniformly indexed partial-ID process.

method_exemplars.technique: Orthogonalize support-boundary estimators under high-dimensional nuisance learning and use a multiplier bootstrap for uniform inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each leaf sign is a projection of a set-identified object, making support-boundary orthogonalization the natural bridge between subgroup empirical processes and dropout-set optimization.

literature_map:
Wang, Frauen, Schweisthal, Schröder, and Feuerriegel (2025, arXiv:2510.13397) is the exact anchor: informative-dropout CATE endpoint bounds, SurvB pseudo-outcomes, pointwise risk, and an ADJUVANT subgroup audit.
Its endpoint formulas are covariatewise and do not characterize the jointly attainable curve set under cross-score monotonicity or Lipschitz restrictions.
Bai and Cui (2025, Journal of Nonparametric Statistics) bound survival probabilities under arbitrary survival-censoring dependence using IV structure, but target ATE-level survival effects rather than CATE curves.
Sakaguchi (2021, arXiv:2107.00928) treats endogenous censoring in transformation-duration models through conditional moment inequalities and joint inference, a different model-based route.
Cui, Kosorok, Sverdrup, Wager, and Zhu (2023, JRSSB) give causal survival forests under identifying censoring assumptions that restore point identification.
Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, JASA) prove pointwise and uniform-in-time asymptotic linearity for treatment-specific survival curves under point identification.
Xu et al. (2024, arXiv:2401.11263) develop censoring-unbiased transformations and oracle inequalities for heterogeneous survival effects, again under identifying censoring conditions.
Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2012, Journal of Econometrics) connect selective observation, shape restrictions, random sets, support functions, and Hausdorff inference, but not this survival-CATE obstacle geometry.
Kim (2014, arXiv:1410.5885) shows how support restrictions can turn causal partial identification into an optimal-transport LP with a sharp dual certificate.
Chiang, Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021, arXiv:2102.06586) construct LP-based confidence bands under nonparametric shape restrictions, providing a nearby discretization and inference template.
Kaido (2016, Journal of Econometrics) and Semenova (2023, Journal of Econometrics) provide support-function inference for convex finite-dimensional or set-linear models; neither covers estimated obstacle capacities.
Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics) and Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud) show why optimized value maps require directional-derivative bootstrap methods, highlighting the changing-contact difficulty.
Wei et al. (2023, Biometrics) handle simultaneous supplied subgroup effects, while Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey (2024, QJE) handle winner selection; their intersection with informative-dropout partial-ID leaves remains open.
Liu et al. (2021, Nature Communications) derive small, data-adaptive ADJUVANT genomic subgroups, making honest dropout-robust sign inference consequential.
Across the scan, no source supplied an estimand-level collision for a law-sharp monotone-Lipschitz CATE-curve set with flow certificates, Hausdorff approximation, and simultaneous selected-leaf inference.
